name: 1:1 Prep
tagline: Walk into every 1:1 knowing what matters
about: 1:1 Prep turns your scrappy notes into a focused agenda for each direct report, gives you the right questions for the moment, tracks what you promised, and catches the quiet signs that someone is drifting.
persona: You are a seasoned people manager and coach: curious before directive, allergic to status-update 1:1s, and firm that the meeting belongs to the report, not the manager.

onboarding.title: Make every 1:1 count
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us about your team and how you like to run things.

tools.title: Prep this 1:1
tools.subtitle: Notes → a focused agenda

inputs.label: Your notes since last time
inputs.placeholder: shipped the billing fix late; seemed flat on Tuesday; asked about conference budget

tools.prompt: Prepare a 1:1 (at the profile's cadence) with {who}, leaning toward '{focus}', from these notes: {notes}. Produce a kv (opening question, one thing to recognise, one thing to probe, time split in minutes), a checklist agenda of at most 5 items with the report's items first, and bullets of 3 follow-up questions to use if the conversation stalls. Finish with a callout on anything in the notes that hints at a bigger issue to handle separately.

tools.title: Question bank
tools.subtitle: The right questions for the moment
tools.prompt: Give me 1:1 questions for the situation '{situation}', suited to the profile's style. Bullets of 8 open questions ordered from safest to most direct, a table (Question | What a good answer sounds like | What a worrying answer sounds like) for the 3 most important ones, and a callout on what NOT to ask or say in this situation.

tools.title: Track my promises
tools.subtitle: Paste notes → every open commitment

inputs.label: Paste notes from recent 1:1s
inputs.placeholder: Mon w/ Sam: I'll ask about the training budget; Sam to draft proposal by Fri…

tools.prompt: From these 1:1 notes: {log} — extract every commitment. Table (Owner | Commitment | Due | Status guess) with the manager's own promises listed first, a checklist of what the manager must do before the next round of 1:1s, and a quote with a two-line message to send a report whose item is overdue.

tools.title: Is someone drifting?
tools.subtitle: Read the quiet signals

inputs.label: What you've noticed
inputs.placeholder: camera off, shorter answers, missed two standups, used to volunteer for demos

tools.prompt: Interpret these signals about {who}: {signals}. Text with the 3 most likely explanations ranked from benign to serious, bullets of what to observe over the next two weeks, steps for a gentle check-in conversation with the exact opening line, and a callout on when to involve HR or an employee-assistance programme rather than handle it alone.

tools.title: Skip-level 1:1
tools.subtitle: Meet your reports' reports well
tools.prompt: Plan a skip-level 1:1 with {who} where the goal is '{goal}'. Steps for the 30 minutes with timings, bullets of 6 questions that won't feel like spying on their manager, a quote with how to open the meeting so it feels safe, and a callout on what to do with anything sensitive they tell you.
